title: Slug generation for URLs

requirements.text: Titles become lowercase URL-safe slugs: accents transliterated, apostrophes joined, punctuation collapsed to one separator
Slugs are truncated to a maximum length at a word boundary
Input with no usable characters yields a configured fallback instead of an empty slug
A taken slug gets the first free numeric suffix (post-2, post-3 ...)
Uniqueness holds under concurrent creation, enforced by a unique constraint scoped to the tenant/collection with retry
Slugs that collide with application routes or reserved words (admin, new, api) are refused
When a slug changes, the old URL permanently redirects to the new one

evidence.name: slugify lowercases, transliterates Latin diacritics, joins apostrophes and collapses punctuation
slugify truncates at a word boundary and hard-cuts a single overlong word
slugify returns the configured fallback when nothing usable remains
a taken slug gets the first free numeric suffix
PGlite: schema applies; ten concurrent creates of one title get distinct slugs via the unique key and retry
ten concurrent creates of the same title get distinct slugs (memory store)
reserved words and route names are refused as exact slugs and skipped when derived
rename keeps history and old slugs resolve to a permanent redirect to the current slug
redirect chains collapse to the current slug and renaming back never loops
PGlite: reserved words, rename history, collapsed redirects and reclaiming an old slug

implementations.notes: Old slugs stay owned by their entity and redirect to the current slug; SQL renames need an executor with transaction(). PGlite tests run on one connection.

uniqueSlug checks a caller-supplied set or predicate; it does not guard against concurrent inserts

notes: Concurrency-safe uniqueness, reserved words and rename redirects are uncovered. module:short-links has reserved words and ON CONFLICT retry for short codes, not for title slugs.
